newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMANY HAS LOST 1,000 BANKS SINCE 1990-BUNDESBANK.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY HAS LOST 1,000 BANKS SINCE 1990-BUNDESBANK.

text.p: Germany's banking sector has shrunk by a fifth since 1990 as closures and mergers reduced the number of banks by more than a thousand, the Bundesbank said Wednesday.

More than 100 banks disappeared in 1996 alone, bringing the total down to 3,517, the central bank said in its August monthly report. About 500 branches were closed last year and employment in the sector fell by about 7,000 to 727,000.

The figures confirm a trend toward consolidation in a sector regarded by analysts as grossly overcrowded and cost-laden. Even Deutsche Bank AG, by far the country's biggest bank, commands a market share of just 5 percent.
Analysts say the blood-letting is far from over and further mergers are in store, particularly as Europe's planned monetary union in 1999 looks set to intensify competition.

Last month's news of a planned fusion between two Bavarian banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG , has triggered intense speculation that further megamergers will follow.

Meanwhile, in a bid to woo customers and cut costs, banks have started opening branches in supermarkets, extended their hours to suit the extension in shopping hours and installed more automatic cash dispensers.
The Bundesbank said that the number of cash dispensers had trebled to about 38,000 since 1990.
